title: Triggers, context variables, before/after events, and trigger frameworks
objectives: Choose before versus after trigger events from record state: mutable Trigger.new before save, read-only after save, Id present after insert.
Use context variables (isBefore, isAfter, operationType, new, old, newMap, oldMap, size) with the official availability rules.
Keep one trigger per object that delegates to a handler class (a trigger framework) instead of unordered duplicate triggers.
Bulkify Trigger.new and never DML Trigger.new/old lists directly.
diagnostic_question: You must stamp a status on LAB_Shipment__c before it is written, then create child LAB_Stop__c rows that need the parent Id. Which trigger events, which context variables, and why not two competing before-insert triggers?
definition: Apex triggers run custom logic before or after record changes—insert, update, delete, merge, upsert, and after undelete. Before triggers update or validate values before the database save. After triggers see system-set fields such as Id and may change other records; the records that fired the after trigger are read-only. Context variables on System.Trigger describe the event and the batch. ([Triggers](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_triggers.htm); [Trigger Context Variables](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_triggers_context_variables.htm))
why_it_matters: Wrong event is the most common trigger interview fail: mutating Trigger.new after save throws; inserting children before the parent Id exists fails; two triggers on the same event have no guaranteed order and share governors (APEX-007).
sixty_second_explanation: Think of airport security. Before the boarding pass is written, agents can still correct the name on the form—that is a before trigger and Trigger.new is writable. After the pass is in the system the barcode (Id) exists, the pass itself is read-only, and you can print bag tags for other records—that is after. The manifest for this group of 200 passengers is Trigger.new, Trigger.old, and operationType. A trigger framework is one doorway per terminal that hands work to handler classes so two doorways do not argue about order.
deeper_explanation: Before triggers run before save and may change Trigger.new field values or addError. After triggers run after save (not yet committed): Id and audit fields exist; Trigger.new is read-only; related DML is typical. After undelete exists; there is no before undelete. ([Triggers](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_triggers.htm))

Context variables: isInsert/Update/Delete/Undelete, isBefore/isAfter, operationType (BEFORE_INSERT … AFTER_UNDELETE), new/newMap/old/oldMap, size. new is available on insert, update, undelete and is writable only in before. newMap is not available in before insert. old is always read-only. Do not DML trigger.new or trigger.old. ([Trigger Context Variables](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_triggers_context_variables.htm); [Context Variable Considerations](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_triggers_context_variables_considerations.htm))

Event-versus-state table (official considerations): before insert may change Trigger.new; after insert cannot, but may update/delete the original via separate DML. before update may change Trigger.new but must not update/delete the original via DML. after update may DML the original (recursion risk). before delete has no Trigger.new. ([Context Variable Considerations](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_triggers_context_variables_considerations.htm))

A trigger framework here means one trigger per object that switches on operationType and calls a handler class. Salesforce does not guarantee order among multiple triggers on the same object and event; they share one governor pool. Recursion and static flags continue with APEX-009/010. Prefer Flow when AUTO-001 says so.

mental_model.analogy: Airport security: correct the form before the boarding pass is written; after the barcode exists the pass is read-only and you print bag tags for other bags.
useful_mapping: before trigger → agents still writing on the paper form (Trigger.new writable)
after trigger → pass is in the system; barcode/Id exists; pass is read-only
Trigger.new → this batch's passenger list (up to 200)
Trigger.old → the previous names on an update/delete
one trigger + handler class → one doorway per terminal (framework)
where_it_breaks: After save is not yet commit; rollback can still erase the pass.
Multiple triggers are not two orderly lanes—order is not guaranteed.
Workflow extra passes (APEX-009) are not a second airport.
The analogy does not encode governor numbers.

teach_back_prompt: Explain before versus after using the boarding-pass idea, then name one place the airport analogy breaks (commit versus save, or unordered triggers).

claims.claim: Before triggers update or validate values before save. After triggers access system-set fields such as Id and affect other records; after-trigger records are read-only.
claims.validation: Triggers topic in the Apex Developer Guide.

claims.claim: Context variables include isBefore/isAfter, operationType, new/old/maps, and size (current batch). new is writable only in before triggers.
You cannot use trigger.new or trigger.old in Apex DML operations. In after triggers, changing Trigger.new is not saved and throws. before update cannot update or delete the original via DML.

telugu_glossary.telugu: Change Trigger.new before the row is saved.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Before: mutate Trigger.new or addError before save; no Id on insert. After: Id exists, Trigger.new is read-only, DML other records. I use operationType and one trigger per object that calls a handler class.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I pick the event from record state, not habit. Same-row stamp is before. Children that need the parent Id are after insert. I never DML Trigger.new. I never update the original in before update. Two triggers on the same event are unordered and share governors, so I use one trigger plus a handler—that is the framework I mean. Recursion and order of execution are APEX-009.

terminology.plain: Apex that runs automatically on a record change event.
terminology.precise: A trigger on an sObject for before/after insert, update, delete, or after undelete (plus merge/upsert participation).
terminology.example: trigger LAB_ShipmentTrigger on LAB_Shipment__c (before insert, after insert) { ... }
terminology.non_example: A record-triggered Flow, which is declarative automation.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Apex class: the handler a trigger should call.
terminology.boundary: Prefer Flow when AUTO-001 says the requirement is declarative.

terminology.plain: Logic that runs before the row is written.
terminology.precise: Trigger.new field values for the current row can be modified; addError can block the save. On insert, Id is not yet available.
terminology.non_example: Inserting child stops that need the parent Id.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Before-save Flow, which runs earlier in APEX-009.
terminology.boundary: Do not DML the original in before update.

terminology.plain: Logic that runs after the row is saved but before commit.
terminology.precise: Id and system fields exist. Trigger.new is read-only. Typical work is related DML or async enqueue.
terminology.example: Insert LAB_Stop__c children after shipment insert.
terminology.non_example: row.Status__c = 'X' on Trigger.new in after context.
terminology.boundary: Extra same-row DML re-enters the save and must be idempotent.

terminology.plain: Trigger.isBefore, Trigger.new, operationType, and the rest of the batch API.
terminology.precise: Implicit System.Trigger members describing the event and the sObject lists/maps for this invocation.
terminology.non_example: A custom checkbox named Is_Before__c on the record.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Limits.getQueries: a governor counter, not trigger context.
terminology.boundary: newMap is not available in before insert.

terminology.plain: One trigger per object that delegates to handler classes.
terminology.precise: A team pattern: a single trigger file switches on operationType and calls an Apex class. It is not a Salesforce product name. It avoids unordered duplicate triggers sharing governors.
terminology.non_example: Three before-update triggers on Account with no agreed order.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: fLib or a named GitHub handler—optional, not official.
terminology.boundary: Frameworks do not replace bulkification or order-of-execution knowledge.

terminology.plain: The new and previous versions of the batch.
terminology.precise: Lists of sObjects. new on insert/update/undelete; old on update/delete. old is always read-only. Do not pass these lists to DML.
terminology.example: for (LAB_Shipment__c row : Trigger.new) { row.Status__c = 'Open'; } // before only
terminology.confusable_neighbor: newMap/oldMap keyed by Id (not in before insert for newMap).
terminology.boundary: size is this batch, not the whole Data Loader file.

when_to_use: When same-row values must be set in a before trigger on Trigger.new before the save.
When child records or other sObjects need the parent Id in an after trigger.
When context variables and operationType must drive a single trigger framework (one trigger plus handler class).
When diagnosing an after-context write to Trigger.new or a DML of Trigger.new/old.
when_not_to_use: Do not use an after trigger to stamp same-row fields on Trigger.new—that throws or is discarded.
Do not use a before insert trigger to insert children that need the parent Id.
Do not add a second Apex trigger on the same event instead of extending the handler class.
Do not use this triggers lesson as a full record-save order-of-execution map (APEX-009) or as a Flow-versus-Apex product choice (AUTO-001).

decision_table.signal: Same-row field must change before the database write.
decision_table.choose: before insert or before update; assign Trigger.new; no extra DML.
decision_table.why: Before triggers exist to update values before save; after Trigger.new is read-only.

decision_table.signal: Child rows need the new parent Id.
decision_table.choose: after insert; list DML of children.
decision_table.why: Id is set by the system save; after triggers are for that state.

decision_table.signal: You are tempted to update Trigger.new via update in before update.
decision_table.not: update Trigger.new or update the original via DML.
decision_table.why: Considerations table: before update cannot DML the original; do not DML trigger.new.

decision_table.signal: A second before-update trigger appears on the same object.
decision_table.choose: One trigger plus handler class (framework); move the logic.
decision_table.not: Two triggers and an assumed order.
decision_table.why: Order among multiple triggers is not guaranteed; they share governors.

limitations: Does not list the full save-order pipeline (APEX-009).
Named handler libraries are conventions, not official product.
Entity-specific field exceptions (fields not set in before) need the entity-considerations page.
security_notes: Triggers often run in system mode; CRUD/FLS is APEX-014.
Do not log Trigger.new payloads with customer PII.
common_mistakes: SOQL inside a loop over Trigger.new.

troubleshooting.symptom: System.FinalException or runtime error that Trigger.new is read-only / already saved.
check: Move the field assignment to before.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: You need update Trigger.new to persist the field.

troubleshooting.symptom: REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING or null parent on child insert.
check: Child DML is in after insert using row.Id.
You did not run it in before insert.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: The lookup API name is the only bug.

troubleshooting.symptom: Logic sometimes runs in a different order after deploy.
check: Multiple triggers on the same object and event.
Consolidate into one trigger plus handler.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: Salesforce sorts trigger files alphabetically as a contract.

production_notes: One trigger per object is the default review standard.

interview_questions.question: Before versus after triggers—how do you choose?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Before: same-row values and validation before save; Trigger.new writable; no Id on insert. After: Id and other records; Trigger.new read-only.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I start from record state, not habit. Stamping Status is before. Child stops that need the parent Id are after insert. I never assign Trigger.new after save. I mention before-save Flow runs earlier (APEX-009) so they hear I do not ignore declarative options.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Shipment__c Status in before insert; LAB_Stop__c in after insert.
weak_answer_warnings: after trigger for every field stamp

interview_questions.question: Name the trigger context variables you actually use.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: operationType, isBefore/isAfter, new, old, newMap, oldMap, size. I switch on operationType and I never DML new/old.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I mention newMap is missing in before insert because Ids do not exist. old is read-only. size is this 200-row batch. isExecuting is rarely useful in interviews compared with operationType. I keep Boolean soup (isBefore && isInsert) as the legacy form.
interview_questions.example: switch on Trigger.operationType { when BEFORE_UPDATE { handler.beforeUpdate(Trigger.new, Trigger.oldMap); } }

interview_questions.question: After-insert code sets Trigger.new[0].Status__c = 'Open' and nothing sticks—or it throws. Why?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: After Trigger.new is read-only and already saved. Stamp in before insert, or issue a separate update in after (and handle recursion).
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I prefer before so I do not burn a DML statement or re-enter the save. If they already used after, I show the considerations table. I do not update Trigger.new as a list. I mention workflow re-entry only as APEX-009.
interview_questions.example: Move the assignment into before insert on Trigger.new.
tradeoffs: Before assignment vs after update DML
follow_ups: What error text do you expect?
Would a formula field be enough?

interview_questions.question: Two before-update triggers on Account disagree after a deploy. How do you fix it?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Order is not guaranteed. Collapse to one trigger that calls a handler class—the framework I mean.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I retrieve both files, move methods into LAB_AccountHandler, delete the extra trigger. I add tests for both behaviors in one 200-row update. I remind them they share governors so two fat triggers are worse than one. I do not rely on filename sort.
interview_questions.example: AccountTrigger plus AccountTrigger2 become AccountTrigger → AccountHandler.
follow_ups: How do you coexist with a package trigger?

interview_questions.question: When would you refuse to write a trigger?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When a before-save Flow or validation rule already does the same-row job safely. Triggers are for bulk Apex that Flow cannot express cleanly.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: AUTO-001 owns the product choice, but trigger interviews still expect judgment. I refuse a trigger that only sets one field Flow can set. I refuse a second trigger. I write a trigger when I need maps, complex related DML, or reuse from a handler class. I still bulkify.
interview_questions.example: Stamp a status: Flow. Split shipments into stops with maps: after-insert handler.

interview_questions.question: Walk the official event-versus-state rules for DML on the original record.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: before insert: N/A. after insert: update/delete allowed. before update: DML on original forbidden. after update: update allowed, recursion risk. before delete: update allowed, delete forbidden. after delete: N/A.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat the considerations table as the interview source. The memorable bits: do not DML Trigger.new/old; do not DML the original in before update; after update same-row DML re-enters and must be idempotent. I do not recite unofficial blog tables.
interview_questions.example: before update: row.Status__c = 'X'; not update row;
follow_ups: Why would you update in before delete?
What happens if you delete in after insert?
weak_answer_warnings: Inventing a before undelete DML rule

interview_questions.question: Child insert in before insert fails. Walk the diagnosis.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The parent Id does not exist yet. Move the child DML to after insert and bulkify.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I confirm the event in the debug log. I collect parent Ids from Trigger.new in after insert and insert a list of children. I do not query the parent back one-by-one. If they used after insert but still have null lookups, I check they used row.Id and the correct relationship field.
tradeoffs: One child per parent vs aggregate
follow_ups: What if the child has its own trigger?
weak_answer_warnings: Inserting children in a loop in before insert

interview_questions.question: What do you mean by a trigger framework, and what is it not?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: One trigger per object, switch on operationType, handler class. It is a team pattern, not a Salesforce SKU. It does not replace bulkification or order of execution.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I contrast three raw triggers with one doorway. I show recursion control and bypass flags as handler concerns, not as a reason to add more trigger files. I refuse to treat a specific GitHub library as official. I keep APEX-009 for the save pipeline.
tradeoffs: Thin trigger vs logic in the trigger file
Domain layer vs one god handler
follow_ups: How do you unit-test a handler without DML?
Where does the static bypass live?
weak_answer_warnings: Naming a blog framework as if it were platform product
